meta.title: WillFolks — Put your money where your goals are
meta.description: Stake USDC on your goals. Hit them and it's yours; miss them and it stays locked for a while, never lost. Alarms, screen time, location and friend-judged goals, held in an escrow contract on Monad.

hero.subtitle: Stake USDC on your habits. Hit the goal and it's yours again. Miss it and it stays locked for a while. Never lost, only locked.

stake.title: Stake
stake.body: Pick a goal and lock real money on it. Your stake sits in an on-chain escrow, out of reach until the goal resolves.

prove.title: Prove
prove.body: Your phone's sensors, a friend acting as judge or an AI agent check whether you actually did it. A signed verdict settles it on-chain.

keep.title: Keep
keep.body: Did it? The money is yours, withdraw whenever. Didn't? It stays locked for a set period, then it's yours again.

win.title: You hit it
win.body: Stake released. Withdraw any time, keep the streak, feed the pet.

miss.title: You miss it
miss.body: Stake locked for the penalty period. We never keep it: when the lock ends, it comes back.

features.sectionTitle: Six ways to keep your word

escrow.title: Escrow on Monad
escrow.description: Stake USDC on your goals in an escrow contract on Monad. Complete them and withdraw anytime. Miss them and your funds stay locked for a set period. Never lost, only locked.

alarm.title: Smart Alarms
alarm.description: Set wake-up alarms backed by real money. Miss your alarm? Your stake gets locked. Consistency pays — literally.

appTimer.title: App Timer
appTimer.description: Limit your screen time on distracting apps. Set weekly limits and put money on the line. Your wallet keeps you focused.

locator.title: Location Tracker
locator.description: Set location-based goals. Arrive on time to the gym, office, or class. Your GPS verifies, your wallet rewards.

unmeasurable.title: Friend & AI Judges
unmeasurable.description: Goals sensors can't measure, like homework or chores, are judged by a friend you trust or by an AI agent that checks your photo proof.

deposits.title: Built-in USDC Wallet
deposits.description: A wallet created on your phone holds your USDC. Every stake and payout is a transaction you can check on the explorer. Local-currency deposits are next.

faq.title:
Fair
questions.
faq.a1: WillFolks is a commitment app: you create a goal (wake up early, limit app usage, arrive somewhere on time, finish a chore) and lock a stake in USDC. Meet the goal and the money is yours to withdraw at any time. Miss it and the stake stays locked for a set period as a penalty.
faq.q2: How does the Escrow mechanism work?
faq.a2: When you create a goal, your stake moves from your own wallet into the WillFolksEscrow contract on Monad. A verdict signed by an authorised attestor tells the contract whether you made it, and the contract releases or locks the funds. If nobody resolves the goal, you can reclaim the stake yourself.
faq.q3: What happens if I miss a goal or an alarm?
faq.a3: If you don't complete the goal (for example, you sleep through an alarm or go over your screen-time limit), the stake stays locked for the penalty period. It is never kept by us: once the lock ends, it is yours again.
faq.q4: How are goals verified if they don't use sensors?
faq.a4: Goals your phone can't measure, like studying or chores, are judged by a friend you pick or by an AI agent that reviews your photo proof. Today the friend judge is real and the AI judge is still a simple stand-in.
faq.q5: What deposit and withdrawal methods does the app support?
faq.a5: Today you stake test USDC on Monad testnet with a wallet created on your phone, plus free test funds once a day. Deposits in local currency, so you can enter and leave without touching crypto, are on the roadmap.
faq.a6: Not yet. WillFolks runs on Monad testnet with test USDC and a cap of 10 USDC per goal while the contract is unaudited. You can try the whole flow without risking anything.

steps.title: Try it in five steps
steps.note: Everything runs on Monad testnet; no real money is involved.

items.title: Install & sign in
items.body: Install the Android app from the GitHub releases and sign in with any email (development login).

items.title: Get test funds
items.body: Open Wallet and tap "Get test balance": you get 3 test USDC plus gas to use them.

items.title: Stake a goal
items.body: Create an Alarm goal with a 1 USDC stake and tap "Stake it". The goal shows the stake as "Stake in play" with a link to the transaction.

items.title: Watch it resolve
items.body: Demo goals last about 5 minutes. When they end, the stake returns and the Wallet history shows the transaction.

items.title: Try any goal
items.body: You can create any type of goal; depending on which one, it can take a reasonable amount of waiting time to resolve.

limits.title: Said plainly
items: Unaudited contract, testnet only, capped at 10 USDC per goal.
One attestor (our backend) signs verdicts today; a quorum of verifiers is planned for a later phase.
Alarm and app-usage results are reported by the phone and trusted by the server.
The AI judge is a stub that approves any photo; the friend judge is real.
Fiat deposits and bank withdrawals are not live yet; sign-in is a development login.

pitch.title:
Put your money
where your goals are.
pitch.lede: Why commitment works, why people still drop it, and how WillFolks makes keeping your word the easiest move, in a few minutes.
points: The problem: everyone sets goals, few keep them, and commitment tools get abandoned.
The product: stake USDC on a goal, prove it with your phone, keep your money.
Why Monad: cheap, fast transactions that make small everyday stakes possible.
The business: no profit from failure, revenue from money moving through the product.
What is live today and what comes next.

gtm.title:
Go-to-
market.
gtm.lede: Who tries WillFolks first, how they find it, what we need to learn before scaling, and how the product makes money without profiting from anyone failing.
gtm.pull: We do not profit from users failing: a stake is only ever locked, never kept.

sections.title: First users
body: People who already hold USDC and use wallets: Monad and EVM builder communities. They can try the product today, give honest feedback, and understand a commitment contract instantly.
We treat them as early adopters, not the mass market. Mainstream users will be validated separately with a small-deposit or fiat flow.

sections.title: How they find us
body: Building in public from day 0: a weekly update with a short clip and a link to the code, one technical post per week, and showing up in builder Discords and Telegram groups to be useful before asking for anything.
A seven-day open challenge with testnet USDC gives the community a reason to try it together.

sections.title: What we will learn first
body: The real risk is not interest but adoption and retention: people often sign up for commitment tools and then drop them. We write the success thresholds down beforehand and change segment or message if we miss them.

sections.title: Why people stay
body: Friends can act as judges, there is a pet that reacts to progress, and a home-screen widget keeps the stake in view.
The money is never lost, only locked, which lowers the fear of starting.

sections.title: Business model
body: Revenue is planned from three places tied to money moving through the product, so our income grows with the money users commit, not with their mistakes.

list.title: Exchange spread
list.body: A small margin when users convert local currency to USDC and back, so people can enter and leave without touching crypto.

list.title: Deposit fees
list.body: A small, visible fee on deposits, whether they arrive in crypto or through a local payment method.

list.title: Share of the yield
list.body: While a stake is locked it can earn yield; the user keeps most of it and we take a percentage.

sections.after: Later, challenges for communities and teams and a verification service other apps can pay for add revenue that does not depend on user balances.
